purpose: ML-E Final ML Certification: verdict + safest wording for every claim that could plausibly be made about PlainCents V2's ML work, so no claim outruns its evidence tier.

verdict_legend.SUPPORTED: Directly established by committed evidence, as stated.
verdict_legend.SUPPORTED_WITH_QUALIFICATION: True only with a stated limitation attached; the limitation must travel with the claim.
verdict_legend.NOT_SUPPORTED: Evidence does not establish this; must not be claimed.

claims.claim: PlainCents V2 categorizes transactions using TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.
claims.safest_wording: PlainCents V2's production categorizer is TF-IDF + Logistic Regression, selected via evidence-based comparison against K-Means and Linear SVM.
claims.limitation: None — this is a direct statement of the shipped implementation, verified via runtime equivalence (ML-E A).

claims.claim: PlainCents V2 uses evidence-based model selection.
claims.safest_wording: Model selection followed a documented protocol: frozen merchant-grouped/temporal splits, TRAIN-only fitting, VALIDATION-based comparison, and a single held-out FINAL evaluation of the selected candidate only.
claims.limitation: The protocol is rigorous; the underlying benchmark sample sizes are still small (Tier B: 228 rows total; forecasting: synthetic).

claims.claim: PlainCents benchmarked K-Means, Logistic Regression, and Linear SVM.
claims.safest_wording: Three categorization candidates were benchmarked on the same frozen TRAIN/VALIDATION split: K-Means (isolated re-fit), TF-IDF + Logistic Regression, and TF-IDF + Linear SVM.
claims.limitation: None.

claims.claim: Categorization evaluation used merchant-group separation.
claims.safest_wording: The categorization split assigns every transaction sharing a normalized merchant identity to exactly one of TRAIN/VALIDATION/FINAL_TEST, preventing a model from succeeding merely by memorizing a merchant string seen during training.
claims.limitation: None.

claims.claim: Merchant groups do not overlap TRAIN/VALIDATION/FINAL.
claims.safest_wording: Verified structurally (empty pairwise intersections) both in ML-B's own runner and as a defense-in-depth assertion inside ml/categorization/run_final.py and scripts/build_production_logreg_model.py.
claims.limitation: None.

claims.claim: PlainCents achieved 42.2% categorization accuracy.
claims.safest_wording: On a 45-row, 17-merchant-group held-out FINAL_TEST slice of an independently curated Tier B benchmark, the selected LogReg model scored 42.2% accuracy — a single, small-sample measurement, not a production accuracy guarantee.
claims.limitation: n=45 rows / 17 merchant groups. Not real-world bank-transaction data. A single held-out measurement, not a distribution.

claims.claim: PlainCents achieved 0.4405 macro F1.
claims.safest_wording: Macro F1 of 0.4405 on the same 45-row Tier B FINAL_TEST slice described above.
claims.limitation: Same small-sample/Tier-B limitation as the accuracy figure; per-category F1 ranges from 0.22 to 1.0 across only 4-9 support rows per category.

claims.claim: PlainCents categorizes real-world bank transactions at 42.2% accuracy.
claims.safest_wording: Do not make this claim. Say instead: 42.2% accuracy on a curated Tier B benchmark (not real-world bank data).
claims.limitation: Tier B is an independently curated/constructed benchmark (ML Spec Section 3.2), explicitly not real-world bank export data. No real bank CSV has ever been scored.

claims.claim: PlainCents V2 forecasting achieved approximately 18.9% WAPE.
claims.safest_wording: On a reserved 3-month period (2024-10/11/12) of a synthetic 24-month dataset, the selected Naive forecaster scored 18.87% combined WAPE.
claims.limitation: Fully synthetic dataset (data/raw/synthetic_24mo.csv), categorized by the production K-Means artifact read-only. Never real spending data.

claims.claim: PlainCents forecasts real-world personal spending at approximately 18.9% WAPE.
claims.safest_wording: Do not make this claim. Say instead: 18.9% WAPE on a synthetic 3-month reserved evaluation period — a mechanism/behavior check, not a real-world accuracy figure.
claims.limitation: Evidence tier is synthetic throughout (ML Spec Section 3.1/21) — no real transaction history has ever been forecast-evaluated.

claims.claim: Naive forecasting outperformed RF/Ridge under the frozen synthetic validation protocol.
claims.safest_wording: Across 14 expanding-window VALIDATION origins, Naive's mean WAPE (0.191) was lower than every RF/Ridge variant tested (0.235-0.257), and Naive beat Seasonal Naive in 11/11 comparable origins.
claims.limitation: Synthetic evidence tier; a 14-origin sample.

claims.claim: Random Forest was rejected because it failed to consistently beat the required baseline.
claims.safest_wording: RF (both strategies) beat Naive in fewer than half of the 14 VALIDATION origins (last-known-history: 6/14; recursive: 4/14), so the ML Spec's Section 14 rule selected the simpler Naive baseline instead.
claims.limitation: None beyond the synthetic evidence tier already noted.

claims.claim: V2 categorization improved over V1.
claims.safest_wording: Do not claim a V1-to-V2 accuracy improvement. V1's 90% figure and V2's 42.2% figure come from different, non-comparable evidence tiers (V1: same-distribution synthetic keyword-labeled diagnostic; V2: independently curated Tier B benchmark with merchant-group separation) — a lower V2 number reflects a harder, more honest test, not a regression.
claims.limitation: The two numbers are not on the same scale and must never be subtracted or ratioed against each other.

claims.claim: V2 categorization generalizes to unseen merchants.
claims.safest_wording: The FINAL_TEST evaluation specifically measures performance on merchant groups never seen during fitting (that is the point of the merchant-grouped split); the selected model scored 42.2% accuracy under that condition.
claims.limitation: "Generalizes" should not be read as "generalizes well" — 42.2% on 8 categories is well above chance (~12.5%) but far from production-grade.

claims.claim: Logistic Regression outperformed K-Means on the Tier B validation set.
claims.safest_wording: On VALIDATION, LogReg scored 0.2552 macro F1 / 32.0% accuracy versus K-Means's 0.0566 macro F1 / 12.0% accuracy (statistically indistinguishable from the ~12.5% random-chance floor for 8 categories).
claims.limitation: None.

claims.claim: TD CSV support is verified against a real TD export.
claims.safest_wording: Do not make this claim. Say instead: fixture-tested against synthetic files shaped like TD's documented export format, not verified against an actual TD account export.
claims.limitation: No real TD export has ever been used in this repo.

claims.claim: TD CSV support is fixture-tested against publicly researched TD format assumptions.
claims.safest_wording: TD import is tested against synthetic fixtures (clean, unparseable-date, unrecognized-format, duplicate-row variants) shaped like TD's publicly documented export columns — not field-verified against a real export.
claims.limitation: Format assumptions are researched, not field-confirmed.

claims.claim: PlainCents uses real bank transaction data for ML evaluation.
claims.safest_wording: Do not make this claim. Categorization evidence is an independently curated Tier B benchmark (not a real bank export); forecasting evidence is fully synthetic.
claims.limitation: No real bank transaction data has ever been used anywhere in this repo's ML evaluation.

claims.claim: PlainCents uses synthetic data for forecasting evaluation.
claims.safest_wording: Forecasting evaluation uses data/raw/synthetic_24mo.csv (779 synthetic transactions, 24 months), categorized read-only by the production K-Means artifact.
claims.limitation: None — this is an accurate, disclosed limitation, not an overclaim.

claims.claim: PlainCents preserves user corrections separately from model predictions.
claims.safest_wording: predicted_category is written once at import/creation time and is immutable thereafter; a user correction writes confirmed_category instead, and effective_category = COALESCE(confirmed_category, predicted_category) — the original prediction is never overwritten.
claims.limitation: None.

claims.claim: PlainCents automatically retrains from user corrections.
claims.safest_wording: Do not make this claim. There is no online learning: a correction only ever writes confirmed_category; CategorizationService's model artifact is fit offline (scripts/build_production_logreg_model.py) and never refit at request time or on correction.
claims.limitation: Verified directly by tests asserting predict()/predict_batch() never call .fit()/.fit_transform().

claims.claim: (existing README ML claim, pre-ML-D)
claims.safest_wording: The pre-ML-D README described the running categorizer/forecaster as V1's K-Means/Random Forest "used as-is" pending a separate scientific-evaluation milestone. That milestone (ML-B/C/D/E) is now complete and the README has been updated accordingly (see README.md's V2 architecture and Model artifact sections) to describe the selected TF-IDF + Logistic Regression / Naive implementations.
claims.limitation: The old text is now historically inaccurate if left unchanged — it has been updated as part of ML-E, not left as a dangling claim.

claims.claim: (existing project-description ML claim, pre-ML-D)
claims.safest_wording: No separate "project description" document exists outside README.md and docs/ in this repo; the same update applied to README.md resolves this claim category too.
claims.limitation: If a project-description document is later added (e.g. a portfolio site entry), it must be checked against this claim matrix before publishing.
